correctness.rationale: Both inverse inputs have rank-one positive semidefinite symmetric parts and nonzero determinants. The total matrix H has exactly computed determinant, trace of H^T H, and singular-value sum/difference, giving the exact norm for all invertible configurations. Direct graph inversion proves the singular endpoint and full paramonotonicity dichotomy. The determinant and numerator yield a path-uniform quadratic blow-up; the resolvent identity and analyticity of (I+H)^-1 yield the sharp first-order cusp in operator norm. All hypotheses and boundaries are explicit in RESULT.md. CHECKER.py passed 72 exact-rational cases plus 3 asymptotic probes. Finite checks alone would not suffice but the complete symbolic argument does.

value.rationale: The object is the natural full family of planar rank-one dissipations plus skew rotations, a canonical minimally nonparamonotone class. The theorem is a complete classification including an intrinsic singular graph boundary and all parameter regimes, not a numerically chosen narrow example. Its sharp quadratic sensitivity of the parallel-sum map combined with sharp linear stability of the proximal resolvent provides structurally meaningful constants for monotone inclusion computations. Generic inverse conditioning and resolvent nonexpansiveness alone do not give these leading constants or the precise paramonotonicity transition.
